title: Backstop Directive Schema v1
description: Schema for directives — atomic units of committed work that form the project backlog. Position in BACKLOG.yml determines priority. Each directive cites source artifacts and progresses through queued → active → specced → done.

status.description: Lifecycle status. queued = committed but not started. active = work in progress. specced = spec exists. done = implementation complete, gate passed. replaced = superseded by a named successor (requires replaced-by). canceled = work abandoned. No deprecated state for directives.

source.description: Source artifacts that authorized this directive. At least one required. Traceability: 'why is this in the backlog?' must always be answerable. Values are artifact IDs (BUNDLE-NNN, ISSUE-NNN, ADR-NNNN) or session timestamps.

spec.description: SPEC-NNN reference once the directive has been specced. Required when status is specced or done.

completed.description: Completion date. Required when status is done.

specced.description: At specced status, the directive must reference the spec that implements it

done.description: At done status, the directive must have a spec reference and completion date

enforcement.source-required: Every directive must cite at least one source artifact. Lineage must be traceable.
enforcement.position-is-priority: Priority is not a field on the directive. Priority is determined by position in BACKLOG.yml.
enforcement.no-orphan-directives: A directive without a source is rejected. 'Why is this in the backlog?' must always be answerable.
